title: Vector/rerank oddity - quick debugging breadcrumbs
content:
Context:
- Intermittent spikes on /v1/rerank endpoint (90th/99th increase) during small-batch rerank jobs (~8-12 items).
- Some requests return a short embedding vector (length 128) while expected model returns 1536. Not all requests; seems correlated with latency spikes.
- First saw at ~2026-03-10 after deploy of rerank-proxy v1.3.2 (PR 418).

What I saw (timeline):
- 2026-03-10 11:02: spike detected by console alerting (p90 > 1.2s for 10m).
- 2026-03-10 11:04 first erroneous response recorded in S3 logs (small vector).
- 2026-03-10 11:07 Canary rollback to previous proxy stopped most spikes but not all; suggests race in proxy + vector-service compatibility.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Model selection fallback: proxy falls back to a lower-dim model under overloaded routing (e.g., tiny-sim instead of sim-large). Routing table shows weight-based fallback which could choose a cheaper model when capacity is low.
2) Truncated response due to upstream connection close (socket cut) -> client sees partial payload and JSON parser returns shorter array.
3) Vector-store (qdrant/milvus) metadata mismatch returns different dimension declared for collection; rerank logic trusts collection metadata and synthesizes a short vector in some code path.
4) Memory corruption / quantization pipeline bug producing wrong embedding length occasionally (less likely).

Commands and traces I ran (raw):
- curl against proxy to reproduce (used local test token):
  curl -s -X POST https://proxy.internal/v1/rerank -H 'Authorization: Bearer TEST' -d '{"query":"sample q","candidates":["a","b","c"]}' | jq .
  -> returned: {"scores":[0.52,0.41,0.07], "embeddings":[[0.1,0.2,...]]}  (ok)

- Captured failing case by replaying logs:
  # mimicking original client (python requests)
  python -c "import requests,json; r=requests.post('https://proxy.internal/v1/rerank',json={'query':'edge case','candidates':['x']},headers={'Authorization':'Bearer TEST'}); print(r.status_code); print(r.text[:400])"
  -> 200
  -> {"scores":[0.99],"embeddings":[[0.12,0.03]]}   (embedding length 2)

- Verified model-serving direct call to embeddings endpoint at same time window (no anomalies):
  curl -s -X POST https://models.internal/v1/embeddings -H 'Authorization: Bearer INTERNAL' -d '{"model":"sim-large","input":["x","y"]}' | jq '.data[0].embedding | length'
  -> 1536

- Checked proxy logs around 2026-03-10 11:04: (snips)
  INFO [rerank-proxy] request=abc123 route=sim-large backend_req=ok backend_resp=ok backend_dim=1536 latency=412ms
  WARN [rerank-proxy] request=abc123 backend_partial=true socket_closed_by_upstream
  INFO [rerank-proxy] request=abc123 returning_emb_len=2

- Heap/proc snapshot of proxy container at spike: memory usage normal, no OOM.

Quick root-cause pointers from code reading:
- proxy/src/handlers/rerank.go has logic that post-processes backend embeddings. If backend_resp includes "partial":true it still attempts to normalize vector by slicing to declared dimension in config, but then falls back to using "infer-from-payload" path which does a naive len() check and will keep whatever length (bug).
- model-routing table in proxy config has fallback rule: when backend latency > 500ms prefer sim-small (dim 128) for throughput. However, logs show backend chosen was sim-large; fallback not triggered.

Reproduction plan (next steps):
1) Add stricter validation at proxy: if retrieved embedding length != expected_dim then reject and log full payload + upstream headers.
2) Re-run canary with increased logging for backend_resp and socket events; capture raw TCP traces for suspect requests.
3) Add unit test to simulate truncated JSON body from model-serving and ensure proxy returns 5xx instead of silently returning wrong vector.
4) Add quick mitigation: treat backend_partial=true as hard error for 2 releases.
5) Audit any code paths that synthesize vectors (there are two small helper functions in util/vec.go).

Notes on observed correlation with latency spikes:
- Spikes appear when batch sizes go up on hosted nodes and a few backends report slow disk (nvme queueing). This increases socket timeouts on backend clients and we see partial responses.
- Also noticed connection reuse pool size change in rerank-proxy v1.3.2: default keepalive reduced from 90s to 15s -> more frequent connection churn. Could expose race where reading a prior response is misattributed to current request.

Quick fix applied (local):
- Patched handler to check len(embedding) and compare with expected_dim; return 502 if mismatch. Deployed to canary.
- Observed drop in "short vector" incidents in canary for 24h. Still monitoring aggregated metrics.

Log snippets (sanitized):
- failing raw payload (truncated):
{"scores":[0.99],"embeddings":[[0.12,0.03],"__truncated__"
-> JSON parse succeeded because proxy treats trailing broken token as string in some path (weird).

Open questions / to confirm:
- Which component is setting backend_partial flag? (proxy client or model-serving wrapper?)
- Does load balancer/proxy terminate keepalive early and cause half-close leading to partial body? Check infra TCP logs.
- Are there any users of the rerank API who rely on variable-dimension embeddings? Should be no, but search repo for any code that tolerates it.

Useful references / where I looked:
- rerank-proxy handlers and http client code (src/handlers/*, src/httpclient/*)
- infra LB healthcheck and keepalive config (infra/terraform/lb-main.tf)
- SRE notes on nvme queueing incidents in March (confluence: CARD-308)

Next immediate actions (today):
- [ ] Push validation-only patch to canary + alert if mismatch rate > 0.1%
- [ ] Grab raw TCP dump for request abc123 around 2026-03-10 11:04
- [ ] Confirm whether any other services changed keepalive defaults in the March deploy window
- [ ] Loop in Mika (platform) and Aisha (serving) for quick sync

If this turns out to be a parsing bug: prefer 502 and early fail rather than silent return of wrong-dim embedding (user-visible correctness > availability).

Notes to self (personal):
- Remember to grep logs for "returning_emb_len" across clusters (we only saw it on east-1).
- Check telemetry for requests where client sends batch size > 16; maybe different code path.

End of breadcrumb.
